summary: Personal AI assistant you run locally or in the cloud, with long-term memory, skills, plugins and chat app connections.

heroCommands.command:
pip install qwenpaw
qwenpaw init --defaults
qwenpaw app

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: QwenPaw is a personal AI assistant from the AgentScope team. You deploy it on your own machine or in the cloud, extend it with skills and plugins, and talk to it from chat apps like DingTalk, Lark and WeChat.
sixtySeconds.problem: Most assistants forget past conversations and live only in the cloud. QwenPaw keeps a three-layer memory, can run a local model with no API key, and blocks dangerous commands before they run.
whoFor: People who want a self-hosted assistant
Teams using DingTalk, Lark or WeChat
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for built-in local models (QwenPaw-Flash) that run without an API key, strong security guards, multi-agent support and many channels.
requirements: Python 3.11 to 3.13 for pip install, or use the install script

overview: Install with pip (then qwenpaw init --defaults and qwenpaw app) or with a one-line script for macOS/Linux or Windows that sets up uv and a virtual environment for you. Open the console at http://127.0.0.1:8088/ to configure your model.

Memory has three layers: live working context, full history and a self-evolving knowledge base. QwenPaw-Flash models (2B to 35B) run through the built-in local runtime, or you can use cloud providers.

Security features include a kernel-level sandbox, tool and file guards, a skill scanner and access policies. You can spawn sub-agents and use the Agent Communication Protocol. The project is Apache 2.0 licensed.
